items.title: Growth Lead, Japan
items.description: About the Team The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows. The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements. We combine product strategy with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets. About the Role We’re looking for a growth lead in Japan to shape and execute ChatGPT’s growth plans. You’ll partner with the Japan GM to understand local users, identify the biggest growth opportunities, and turn those priorities into product improvements, funnel optimizations, and performance marketing tests. You’ll work across acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization, collaborating with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Partnerships, and Marketing teams to influence priorities and ship measurable impact. The role combines product growth and funnel optimization with performance marketing: connecting audience, message, creative, and channel learnings to better in-product journeys. In this role, you will: - Partner with the Japan GM to set a country growth plan and roadmap priorities, with clear hypotheses, owners, dependencies, and measurable outcomes. - Use user research, funnel and cohort data, and competitive insight to find local friction and prioritize the opportunities that matter most to users. - Run performance marketing tests in collaboration with regional marketers across relevant channels, creators, and partners; use incrementality, CAC, payback, and LTV to decide what to scale. - Design and run rigorous experiments across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, and paid conversion; measure incremental impact and iterate. Work with Product, Engineering, Design, and Data Science partners to prototype, test, and ship locally relevant experiences. - Partner with regional Marketing and central media teams to brief and prioritize audience, positioning, creative, and channel tests based on the country plan. - Own the country growth scorecard across acquisition, retention, paid conversion, and unit economics, distinguishing incremental user and revenue gains and learnings Connect priority use cases, product improvements, and acquisition plans into a coherent journey from first exposure to repeated value. - Run the growth operating cadence with the GM and regional teams, aligning central and local partners on results, trade-offs, dependencies, and next steps. - Build and operate segmentation, lifecycle journeys, growth tooling, performance marketing and product experimentation capabilities that can be scaled across markets. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 10+ years of experience across product growth, growth marketing, data science, or growth strategy and operations, with hands-on execution in a fast-moving technology company. - A user-first track record of turning local research and behavior into product and growth priorities, then shipping improvements with measurable impact. - Strong command of acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization funnels, including technically rigorous experimentation and interpretation. - Practical performance marketing experience across audience, channel, creative, and measurement decisions, and the ability to partner effectively with media specialists. - Analytical fluency in cohort analysis and growth economics, including incrementality, LTV, CAC, payback, and contribution margin. - Experience adapting and running campaigns across markets, using local audience behavior, channels, language, and cultural context to improve relevance and performance at scale. - Experience owning growth goals and delivering measurable user or revenue outcomes across product and marketing levers. - The ability to influence and align central and regional teams, translate local needs into scalable approaches, and make progress through ambiguity. Workplace & Location - Tokyo, Japan - Travel as needed for key cross-functional sprints and regional collaboration. items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is looking for a Customer Marketing Manager to make sure our most important messages are backed by customers who can speak to them. This role works across regions and customer segments on special projects tied to the company's top priorities. When we launch a new model, feature, or initiative, you'll find the customers who can speak to it and get them on the record. We're looking for an excellent communicator who can turn customer stories into multiple formats that flex across channels. This often means working under compressed timelines and leading customer storytelling on some of the most important projects at Anthropic. You'll work closely with Product Marketing, Sales, Brand, Comms, Customer Marketing segment leads, and the writers on our team. The right person has done both product marketing and customer marketing, and has a reporter's nose for a good story. Key responsibilities Own the customer evidence strategy for the company's top priorities, deciding which claims need customer proof, which customers are best placed to back them up, and where we have gaps to close Bring what customers are telling us back to Product Marketing and Sales, so our messaging reflects what lands with buyers Stand up new programs as company priorities shift, setting the scope, the customer list, and the plan to ship quickly Lead the customer plan for major model and product launches, from which customers we engage with to how their voices show up in the announcement Partner with Brand and Creative on which customer stories anchor our campaigns and how we tell them Build proof point libraries and enablement around our key messages, so account teams know which story to use and when Shape the customer narrative our executives use in keynotes, posts, and customer conversations Prioritize customer asks when several teams want to tap the same customer, and work with Comms, Legal, and customer executives to get high-profile stories approved Minimum qualifications Can read a messaging doc and quickly spot what customer proof it needs and where the gaps are Are a strong writer and interviewer who can get a customer to say something specific and true, then turn it into a story people want to read Have supported product launches and campaigns with customer proof, often on tight timelines Have built sales enablement that sales teams kept using after launch week Are comfortable with technical products and can explain/write what a customer built, and why it matters, in plain language Know how to work across a lot of teams without formal authority, and can say “not yet” when a request doesn't fit the plan Have good judgment about when a story is ready and when it needs more work Enjoy moving between very different projects, sometimes in the same week Already use Claude to help with drafts and interview prep Preferred qualifications Have 7+ years in B2B marketing, with time in both product marketing and customer marketing Worked in AI or developer tools A background in journalism or editorial A background in Product Marketing or Messaging Written keynotes or LinkedIn posts for executives Run message testing or win/loss interviews to learn what buyers respond to Worked with Comms or analyst relations on announcements that featured customers The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $255,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Adoption, Innovation, and Transformation (AIT) team within OpenAI for Government helps government organizations turn OpenAI products into durable capabilities and measurable mission impact. We work alongside government leaders and public servants to move from exploration to confident, responsible, organization-wide use of AI, including our Cyber and Daybreak capabilities. Our work combines strategic communications, hands-on enablement, adoption strategy, deployment support, and community building, tailored to government missions and operating environments. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking a Cyber Enablement Lead to help government cyber professionals turn Daybreak’s capabilities into stronger defenses and measurable mission outcomes. This role combines technical credibility, hands-on teaching, strategic communication, and cross-functional leadership. You will own Daybreak’s government product enablement strategy and personally design and deliver the training that brings it to life. Your work will span audience research, curriculum design, recorded demonstrations and courses, hands-on workshops, executive briefings, and cyber councils. You will work directly with U.S. and international government cyber leaders to translate frontier AI capabilities into practical workflows that address operational challenges. You will also partner with the cyber product team, bringing customer feedback, deployment challenges, and adversarial context into product development. Your work will help shape best practices for adopting and deploying our cyber tools, strengthen government cyber defenses, and inform the direction of these capabilities. You will engage across the government cybersecurity ecosystem, including Authorizing Officials (AOs), CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior executives. Practitioners need practical proficiency; executives need a strategic understanding of our cyber products, their value, and their implications for mission and risk. Success means demonstrated capability, sustained adoption, and better cyber outcomes. This role is based in Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel and regular work from government customer sites are required. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Set the vision and own the execution of Daybreak’s government enablement strategy, from audience research and learning objectives to curriculum, delivery, and measurable mission impact. - Serve as a trusted cyber ambassador for OpenAI, leading substantive conversations about our tools and capabilities with U.S. and international government leaders, customers, and the broader cyber community. - Help government leaders understand and respond to AI’s changing cyber landscape through executive briefings, public speaking, and thought leadership grounded in operational experience. - Personally lead technical training, live demonstrations, hands-on workshops, and executive conversations that help AOs, CISOs, cyber operators, developers, and senior leaders apply Daybreak to their work. - Bring frontline experience into product development. Serve as a key point of contact for Daybreak Blue and Red, translating user feedback, deployment friction, and unmet mission needs into actionable product recommendations. - Create practical learning materials, including scripts, recorded demonstrations, interactive labs, digital courses, videos, facilitator guides, and playbooks. - Convene and lead our cyber councils, bringing leaders and practitioners into candid conversations that surface hard questions, share field lessons, and build a community of practice. - Deliver tailored engagements for specialist teams and repeatable learning programs that equip thousands of practitioners to use Daybreak effectively. - Translate frontier capabilities into practical government workflows across the cybersecurity lifecycle, connecting Daybreak’s applications and deployment requirements to challenges such as critical infrastructure security and defense of critical networks. - Develop practical guidance for human-machine teaming in cyber, including where AI adds value, where human judgment is essential, and how teams validate results and act responsibly. - Coordinate across product, security, deployment, and customer teams to address adoption barriers and keep enablement technically accurate, operationally relevant, and current as capabilities and requirements evolve. - Assess demonstrated proficiency, track sustained adoption, and use evidence of stronger cyber performance and mission outcomes to improve programs. items.description: About the Team The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows. The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements. We combine product strategy with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets. About the Role We’re looking for a growth lead in Singapore to shape and execute ChatGPT’s growth plans. You’ll partner with the Singapore GM to understand local users, identify the biggest growth opportunities, and turn those priorities into product improvements, funnel optimizations, and performance marketing tests. You’ll work across acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization, collaborating with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Partnerships, and Marketing teams to influence priorities and ship measurable impact. The role combines product growth and funnel optimization with performance marketing: connecting audience, message, creative, and channel learnings to better in-product journeys. In this role, you will: - Partner with the regional GM to set a country growth plan and roadmap priorities, with clear hypotheses, owners, dependencies, and measurable outcomes. - Use user research, funnel and cohort data, and competitive insight to find local friction and prioritize the opportunities that matter most to users. - Run performance marketing tests in collaboration with regional marketers across relevant channels, creators, and partners; use incrementality, CAC, payback, and LTV to decide what to scale. - Design and run rigorous experiments across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, and paid conversion; measure incremental impact and iterate. Work with Product, Engineering, Design, and Data Science partners to prototype, test, and ship locally relevant experiences. - Partner with regional Marketing and central media teams to brief and prioritize audience, positioning, creative, and channel tests based on the country plan. - Own the country growth scorecard across acquisition, retention, paid conversion, and unit economics, distinguishing incremental user and revenue gains and learnings Connect priority use cases, product improvements, and acquisition plans into a coherent journey from first exposure to repeated value. - Run the growth operating cadence with the GM and regional teams, aligning central and local partners on results, trade-offs, dependencies, and next steps. - Build and operate segmentation, lifecycle journeys, growth tooling, performance marketing and product experimentation capabilities that can be scaled across markets. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 10+ years of experience across product growth, growth marketing, data science, or growth strategy and operations, with hands-on execution in a fast-moving technology company. - A user-first track record of turning local research and behavior into product and growth priorities, then shipping improvements with measurable impact. - Strong command of acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization funnels, including technically rigorous experimentation and interpretation. - Practical performance marketing experience across audience, channel, creative, and measurement decisions, and the ability to partner effectively with media specialists. - Analytical fluency in cohort analysis and growth economics, including incrementality, LTV, CAC, payback, and contribution margin. - Experience adapting and running campaigns across markets, using local audience behavior, channels, language, and cultural context to improve relevance and performance at scale. - Experience owning growth goals and delivering measurable user or revenue outcomes across product and marketing levers. - The ability to influence and align central and regional teams, translate local needs into scalable approaches, and make progress through ambiguity. items.description: Are you ready to get the Easygo Edge? With millions of users across our platforms, fraud prevention here operates at a global scale. As a Junior Fraud Analyst, you run the day to day operations: working alert queues, reviewing accounts and transactions, verifying customer documentation, defending chargebacks and escalating cases that need a senior call. The volume is high and the pace is quick, working to established rules and criteria with a clear audit trail behind every action. What you’ll build with us: The role sits within the Payments Fraud & Risk team, learning directly from its experienced leaders. Beyond the core caseload, there's exposure to live incidents and post incident reviews, and the chance to spot patterns individual alerts don't surface. This is the first step on a fraud prevention career path, with a clear route to Fraud Analyst for those who show accuracy, sound judgement and data led decisions. We know that innovation ignites when we build and create together, in person. This is a full-time opportunity at our Melbourne office. You’ll work right where it all happens, surrounded by our fearless crew shipping high-impact work. Who is Easygo? We’re a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. While they command a fierce global following, our crew is employed directly by Easygo and that’s where the real fun happens. We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast. People who are ready to Unify , Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact. And that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. The impact you’ll make: Work assigned fraud alert, review and verification queues to defined service levels, applying established rules, screening criteria and standard reports Escalate suspicious behaviour or policy violations identified during reviews through the defined escalation route Record complete, accurate case notes and audit trails for every action, handing over each shift cleanly with open cases, volume anomalies and emerging issues documented Build chargeback and payment dispute evidence packs ready for review and submission Resolve fraud related escalations from stakeholders within agreed response times Spot patterns across accounts and cases that individual alerts don't surface, referring them on for deeper analysis Support the team through live fraud incidents and contribute to post-incident reviews, while surfacing procedural gaps and recurring false positives so procedures can be improved Your track record: 1-2 years' experience in fraud, payments, KYC or a comparable operational role Available to work extended hours on a published roster, including a weekend rotation Solid numerical and data literacy, confident in spreadsheets and operational dashboards Attention to detail, with the ability to hold that standard through a high-volume queue Clear, concise written communication Discretion when handling sensitive customer and financial information Bonus points if you also have: iGaming and AML exposure Experience working with large sets of data An understanding of SQL queries Here are our benefits and perks: Sharpening your edge The ultimate sandbox. Help us build our crew and get paid for it with our high-value referral bonus. Because great people know great people. Come as you are and get the Easygo edge.

items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. We're hiring a Senior Staff Software Engineer, Native Mobile to join the App Infra team within the Consumer & Business group as a technical architect for Coinbase's native mobile future. This is the most significant client platform shift in the company's history, replacing the React Native app with native Swift and Kotlin builds for millions of customers. Coinbase mobile engineers will be expected to support both iOS and Android on their teams using AI-driven agentic translation at unprecedented scale. You'll own outcomes spanning the App Infra team and our ~30 product teams, set our architectural patterns, and relentlessly drive Coinbase towards a novel, world-class mobile development experience. What you'll do: Define the technical strategy to make the native app development future at Coinbase a reality. Lead the AI-assisted migration approach, designing reusable AI-automation paradigms such as agent swarms, automated dual-repo synchronization, and continuous improvement of translation efficiency using automated feedback loops. Architect a paved-road native framework in Swift and Kotlin that sets the architectural bar across teams, unlocking the ability for a single mobile contributor to be productive in both iOS and Android codebases simultaneously. Drive organizational readiness as a trusted cross-functional partner with product, design, and engineering leadership, resolving cross-team blockers, de-escalating conflict during the dual-app straddle period, and holding peer leaders to a high bar so their patterns spread across teams. Mentor L5-L6 engineers, develop the technical leadership pipeline for native mobile, and recruit actively through reputation, ensuring the team excels in your absence and your successor is developing. Become a leader throughout the entire mobile community at Coinbase, defining best practices and fostering connection and support between all mobile engineers. Required Skills and Experience: 12+ years of software engineering experience with deep expertise in iOS or Android native mobile development (Swift/iOS or Kotlin/Android) and strong working proficiency in the other platform, operating at depth across your own and adjacent team codebases. Track record of owning outcomes spanning 2-3+ teams that drive business impact, including multi-phase platform migrations or rewrites at scale where you shaped strategy and made trade-offs that raised ROI across teams. Deep mobile performance expertise across iOS and Android, including cold start optimization, frame stability, scroll jank elimination, and device-tier profiling, with experience setting the architectural bar and defining ownership boundaries other teams build against. Proven influence without authority at senior levels, with experience changing the technical direction of teams outside your own, securing leadership alignment on ambiguous high-stakes decisions, and resolving cross-team blockers using all tools at your disposal. items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the team Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits. Within Security GRC, Compliance & Audit Programs runs the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework, the single set of controls that the whole program is built on. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and owns the framework and the assurance view across every control domain. About the role As part of the Security Audit & Controls team, you will own the CCF across every control domain, from access and change management to logging, encryption, and people controls: which controls we have, what each one says, how each maps to the frameworks and commitments we hold, and whether each one is actually working. You'll work with control owners and GRC Partners to draft and validate control descriptions and activities that describe reality rather than policy intent, build the monitoring that shows operating effectiveness continuously instead of once a year, and drive what monitoring finds to closure with control owners. Building with Claude is a normal part of the job: drafting and mapping controls, testing evidence, and monitoring control health, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop. This is an individual contributor role for someone who works well independently, writes clearly, and gets satisfaction from a control set that is accurate, tested, and trusted by auditors and engineers alike. Key responsibilities Own the Common Control Framework: the canonical control set, its mappings to SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and customer commitments, and the change process for adding, retiring, or rewording controls Draft and validate control descriptions and control activities with control owners, so each control states who does what, how often, in which system, and what evidence proves it Design and run continuous monitoring of control efficacy: define the metrics and automated tests that show operating effectiveness, tune out false positives, surface failures to owners before an auditor does, and build the controls maturity model that shows where each control domain stands and what it takes to move up a level Verify remediation and carry it into steady state: GRC Partners lead remediation in their domains and control owners implement the fixes. This role advises on control design and implementation, confirms fixes against what the auditor actually asked for, and keeps one source of truth for control and finding status. Once a fix holds, it works with the partner to standardize the evidence pull and, where appropriate, automate it or build continuous Map new frameworks and commitments onto the CCF as we commit to them, and support gap assessments when a new framework, certification, product, or entity comes into scope, using the CCF as the baseline and writing the requirements for each delta Support the integrated audit and customer audits: readiness checks, walkthrough preparation, evidence request lists, and the readout of external findings back to GRC Evaluate evidence reliability, including the completeness and accuracy of system-generated reports and AI-generated evidence, and set the standard for what audit-ready evidence looks like here Build with Claude: automate control mapping, evidence testing, and monitoring, and verify machine-drafted control language before it becomes the record Minimum qualifications Several years in IT audit, security compliance, or controls assurance, including hands-on ownership of a control framework or control library across more than one framework (for example SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, HIPAA) Working command of audit mechanics: scoping, walkthroughs, sampling, design versus operating effectiveness, deficiency evaluation, and evidence reliability Experience writing control descriptions, control activities, and test procedures that other teams and external auditors relied on Experience with continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence collection, whether you built it, ran it, or audited it Enough technical fluency to read a runbook, a configuration, or a pipeline definition and judge whether it enforces what the written control claims Clear writing, because your control language and status reports are what auditors, engineers, and leadership work from Ability to get control owners and partner teams to prioritize and close work without having authority over them Preferred qualifications Have designed or rebuilt a common controls framework and led the remapping of existing frameworks onto it Have stood up continuous controls monitoring or automated evidence programs and can speak to coverage, false-positive rates, and what changed as a result Have applied LLMs to assurance work, such as control drafting, framework mapping, evidence testing, or monitoring Have defined or assessed controls for AI systems or agents operating in production, or for home-built internal systems Have provided requirements for a homegrown GRC platform and worked with the engineers who build it You don't need to Have done everything on this list. The scarce combination this role exists for is framework ownership plus the judgment to tell whether a control actually works Write production code. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. The RL Scaling team works on how RL scales: what happens to throughput, stability, and learning efficiency as models get larger, episodes get longer, and compute grows by orders of magnitude, and what has to change in our algorithms and systems to keep getting returns from that scale. This role sits squarely across research and engineering. You'll develop next-generation architectures and RL algorithms, take them from a small-scale result to a frontier-scale run, and understand every place they behave differently along the way. You'll build the systems that set how fast the team can iterate: how many experiments, at what scale, and how quickly we can trust the results. And you'll work on Anthropic's largest and fastest RL runs, where the gap between a good idea and a working one is often a problem no one has solved yet. architecture and algorithm variants at meaningful scale Own end-to-end performance of our largest RL runs, from research code down to the hardware Build performance and cost models for proposed architecture and algorithm changes, and use them to decide which ideas get scaled Investigate training dynamics at scale, including instabilities, divergence, and throughput regressions, and trace We're looking for generalists: engineers who can move between these layers, reason from first principles about a system they haven't seen before, and pick the problem that matters most rather than the one closest to their prior experience. You’ll work closely with software engineering, product, design, and business teams from development through launch and ongoing support. This is a unique opportunity to engage directly with the forefront of AI legal issues. This role reports to our DGC of Hardware. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. Maintain deal log accuracy, hit SLAs consistently, and surface observations on recurring approval patterns to the Manager - Flag recurring exceptions to the Director that may signal a gap in the approval framework - Help roll out new commercial policies into the EMEA field by maintaining documentation and supporting enablement sessions What We're Looking For: Experience & Technical Skills - 3 years of experience in a Deal Desk, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or commercial finance role in a B2B SaaS company - Hands-on Salesforce experience — you can navigate opportunity records, run reports, and maintain deal data accuracy without hand-holding - Familiarity with CPQ systems (DealHub, Salesforce CPQ, or similar) — you understand how deal configurations map to pricing outputs - About the role Anthropic's go-to-market engine runs on Salesforce: how leads become pipeline, how deals are tracked and forecast, how customers renew and expand, and how partners work alongside our sellers. As a Business Systems Analyst, you'll be responsible for how one of those core motions is represented in system, and a trusted partner to GTM leadership when they want to change how it works. We're looking for someone who operates at the intersection of three things: a strategist who can sit with GTM leaders and shape how they want to understand their part of the business, an analyst who can turn that into rigorous process and data design, and a builder who's comfortable enough in Salesforce to ship meaningful parts of it themselves. You can move fluidly between whiteboard, requirements doc, and admin console. You'll partner deeply with RevOps on the operating model and with our Salesforce developers on anything that needs code. Where you might sit We're hiring across several parts of the customer lifecycle. Placement depends on your background and where you can have the most impact. Opportunity Acceleration: Owns how deals are tracked, forecast, and credited in Salesforce, from stage design and forecasting to the ownership and team structures behind them. You'll partner with sales leadership to make pipeline something everyone can trust and sellers can work quickly. Lead-to-Pipeline: Owns how leads, inbound demand, and BDR outreach become qualified pipeline: lifecycle stages, routing and ownership, handoff rules, and the tools BDRs and sellers work in every day. You'll partner with BDR, marketing, and sales leadership to make the path from first touch to open opportunity faster and easier to measure. Post-Sales: Owns the systems behind renewals, expansion, and customer coverage: how post-sale opportunities are created, forecast, and worked by account management and customer success. You'll give post-sales leaders a clear, trustworthy view of the customer base and the tools to act on it. Partnerships: Owns how partner-sourced and co-sell deals are registered, attributed, and worked alongside our sellers, including the partner-facing processes and reporting leadership relies on. You'll help turn a fast-growing channel into a motion the business can measure and scale. Key responsibilities Own the design of your core funnel domain in Salesforce: lifecycle stages, process, exit and handoff criteria, key fields, and the automation and guardrails that keep the data trustworthy Partner with GTM leadership on how their motion runs and how they want to see it, and make the tradeoff calls on what teams enter versus what insight that data unlocks Partner with RevOps to systematize how GTM teams are structured, assigned, and credited: ownership, routing, coverage, splits, and the territory and role structures those depend on Operationalize the methodology in system, turning frameworks and process discipline into fields, validation, scoring, and in-context guidance that people actually use Act as data-model steward for your domain and its closest neighbors: the named approver for new fields, automation, and integrations touching those objects, and the keeper of why each one exists Build and ship declarative solutions yourself where that's the right call, and write specs clean enough that our developers can build the rest without five rounds of clarification Own the seams to the neighboring stages of the customer lifecycle (lead handoff, opportunity, quote-to-cash, renewal, partner attribution) so the experience is coherent end to end even where the build sits with another team Evaluate and configure tooling that accelerates the motion: routing, activity capture, sequencing, deal inspection, account planning Run discovery, UAT, enablement, and adoption measurement for everything you ship; help raise the bar for how BSA work is done on this team Minimum qualifications Experience in GTM/Revenue systems as a Business Systems Analyst, Sales Systems Lead, or RevOps Systems role, with real ownership of work in a core funnel domain such as lead management, opportunity and pipeline, renewals and account management, or partner channel Experience designing and rolling out a lifecycle, process model, or forecasting motion at a fast-growing company, owning it from discovery through enablement and adoption Credibility with GTM stakeholders: you've been in the pipeline review, forecast call, or planning session, and you can push back when there's a better answer Hands-on Salesforce skills, with comfort building meaningful parts of your own solution (Flow, validation, assignment and routing, page and Path design) and specs that make the handoff to developers clean Crisp communication across GTM teams, leadership, RevOps, and engineers, adjusting altitude for each Preferred qualifications 5+ years of experience in GTM/Revenue systems roles Salesforce Administrator certification Advanced Administrator, Business Analyst, or Sales Cloud Consultant certification Experience partnering with RevOps or Sales Strategy on team-structure questions (ownership, routing, splits, territory) and turning those decisions into working system design Experience across more than one part of the customer lifecycle, such as lead, opportunity, renewal, or partner Curiosity about AI-assisted systems work and eagerness to fold it into how you design, build, and document; items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role Data Center Security Engineering (DCSE) owns physical security across Anthropic's data center footprint: the sites, the hardware inside them, and the supply chain that delivers it. The Security Fusion Platform is where physical security signals from across that footprint are correlated and put in front of the analysts who act on them. It carries continuous monitoring, audit evidence, metrics, and analyst response, along with the classification and analytics pipelines that turn sensor data into events. You'll build and own the platform analysts work from. This is a foundational role. You'll build the software platform that carries a signal from source to analyst decision, ship its first versions, and keep them running in production. The sensors and systems at each site belong to other DCSE engineers; you define the event contract their owners deliver to, and you build the classification and analytics pipelines that run over what those sources produce. Physical security systems engineers own the operations spaces; you own the software that runs in them. You'll work alongside engineers focused on the sites themselves. What you lead, you own end to end: the design, the technical approach, and the result in production. You'll work with external vendors and integrators, setting requirements and acceptance criteria for what you own and deciding what the team builds itself. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. This role involves regular travel to data center sites. No security clearance is required. These are critical services, and you'll take part in on-call for them. Key responsibilities Design and build the event bus and normalized event schema: source identity, sequencing, health state, and the adapter contract that owners of each sensor and system feed build to, plus adapters where needed Build correlation and alerting: the rules and services that turn events from independent sources into alerts an analyst can act on Build the classification and analytics pipelines: computer vision and multi-sensor fusion, with results landing on the event bus Build analyst surfaces: the queue, escalation tooling, dashboards, camera viewers, and video wall content a items.title: Working Student Deposit Operations (m/f/d)
items.description: Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market. Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns. Team The Synchronised Model Deposit Operations Team is a specialized unit within the Operations Department responsible for the technical and operational management of real-time deposit flows for partners using Portal, Hybrid, and Automation integration models. In these models, the Deposit-taking Bank (DtB) remains the source of truth for the deposit ledger, and the team ensures Raisin’s systems stay aligned with the bank's records. Your Responsibilities Payment & Sync Governance: Execute and supervise real-time automated payment flows. Perform manual interventions and corrective postings under the Four-Eyes Principle to resolve synchronization lags and ensure transaction finality. Data Integrity & Reconciliation: Conduct daily high-frequency reconciliations between internal ledgers and partner bank data. Investigate "out-of-sync" scenarios to ensure permanent data parity and maintain audit-proof documentation. Partner & SLA Management: Serve as the primary operational liaison for Sync Model DtBs. Monitor interface uptime and latency in accordance with regulation, leading root cause analyses for any technical drifts. Technical Integration: Coordinate tech enhancements and system releases. Lead Operational Validation to ensure that technical rollouts maintain system stability and data integrity. Process Optimization: Partner with Product and Tech to refine processes and deposit logic. Provide operational requirements for new features, driving automation and scaling the onboarding of new partners while mitigating Operational Risk (OpRisk). Your Profile Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s program in Business Administration, Data Science, Economics, Law, Marketing, or a related field. Prior internship or practical experience in startups, consulting, or operations is a plus. Early-career candidates and motivated fast-learners are also strongly encouraged to apply. Proficient in Microsoft Excel for data organization and analysis. Comfortable balancing independent problem-solving with close team collaboration. Advanced proficiency (C1 level or higher) in both English and German. Join our mission, join our team – and grow with us! At Raisin, we care about each other and it is one of our top priorities to foster an open and caring environment in which everyone feels welcome and comfortable. Our culture is strongly driven by our ambitious team, which connects more than 75 different nationalities. As part of our team, you will benefit from: Employee Development Budget of €400 and one full training day per year. Flexible working hours, home office and 20 vacation days per year. Do you miss being in the office? The Deutschland Ticket gets you there, which we subsidize with €25 per month. Enjoy more than 50+ different sports with Urban Sports Club: We subsidize your membership with more than €20 per month. Hungry all the time? Snacks, daily fresh fruit as well as drinks provided at the office. Raisin Applicant Privacy Policy We value diversity and the unique experiences each individual brings. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or gender identity.

items.title: Identity and Access Management Analyst
items.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Are you a detail-oriented professional with a passion for identity, access and security compliance? We are looking for a proactive Identity and Access Management Analyst to join our Access and Identity team within Service Operations! In this role, you will make sure the right people have the right access at the right time users across the Group. You will manage the full joiner, mover and leaver lifecycle, administer accounts and permissions across our directory services and applications, and help keep our access controls tight and audit-ready. You will run periodic access reviews, support security audits, and help us automate and improve the way access is managed. Reporting to the Service Operations Manager, you will be based in our Sliema, Malta office on a hybrid basis, splitting your time between office and home. If you thrive in a structured, regulated environment, take initiative, and are eager to grow your IAM expertise, we'd love to hear from you! YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR: - Provisioning, maintaining, reviewing and removing user access and privileges across the joiner, mover and leaver lifecycle. - Administering user accounts, groups and permissions in Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID and connected systems. - Granting or denying access requests based on user role, privileges and company policy, and escalating exceptions. - Applying and maintaining access controls such as SSO, MFA and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). - Conducting periodic access reviews with system owners and Information Security, and following up on remediation. - Investigating access anomalies and permission issues, and escalating potential security concerns. - Supporting internal and external audits with clear, accurate access evidence. - Working with application teams and business analysts to understand access requirements and define role structures. - Ensuring access requests are handled within SLAs and that users are kept updated on their progress. - Producing reports on IAM activity. - Documenting IAM processes and procedures in Confluence and keeping them up to date. - Identifying and delivering improvements to IAM processes and tools, including automation opportunities. - Providing guidance and training to colleagues on how to request and manage access. - Participating in IAM projects and initiatives. - Performing other duties as assigned. OUR SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE THE FOLLOWING: ESSENTIAL SKILLS: - Experience in IAM, IT service management or systems administration. - Understanding of identity lifecycles, least privilege and separation of duties. - Hands-on experience with Active Directory and/or Microsoft Entra ID. - Familiarity with IAM protocols such as SAML, OAuth and OIDC. - Data reporting skills (PowerShell, SQL, Excel). - Experience working with AIM tools, Jira and Confluence. - Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills. - Attention to detail and the ability to follow processes and procedures while maintaining clear audit trails. - Good command of written and spoken English, and the ability to explain access matters to technical and non-technical colleagues. - The ability to work independently and as part of a team. - A quick learner who is willing to improve their own skills continuously and adapt to change in a fast-moving environment. NICE TO HAVE: - Experience in a regulated industry such as online gaming, fintech or financial services, or with ISO 27001 audits. - A Microsoft SC-300 or similar identity or security certification. BENEFITS - 4 weeks of Workation (T&C apply) - Well-being allowance to support your active lifestyle - Private health insurance - Discounts across a range of retailers, gyms, bars & restaurants - We offer an employee assistance program that can provide help and guidance during challenging moments. JOIN US! In our pride, we empower our teammates to find their roar and run with their wildest ideas. We don’t wait for things to happen; we pounce and make it happen! Would you be a good fit for the Leo Pride - give us a roar! As our company working language is English, we’d like to see your CV in English, please

items.title: Connectivity and Cloud Architect
items.description: We are seeking a skilled Connectivity and Cloud Architect to join our Infrastructure area. You will design, implement, and maintain robust network architectures across hybrid on-premise and AWS cloud environments, with a strong focus on routing (BGP), connectivity, and DNS architecture, working closely with our Enterprise Architect, infrastructure, and network teams to ensure seamless integration and optimal performance across all systems. A taster of what you will be involved with: Network Architecture Design: Design and develop scalable, secure network architectures across hybrid on-premise and AWS cloud environments, including routing, connectivity, and integration patterns. AWS Network Architecture: Lead design and implementation of AWS networking components, including Transit Gateways, VPC connectivity, ACLs, Network Firewalls, Cloud WAN, and Route 53. Hybrid Connectivity: Design and manage AWS Direct Connect and Site-to-Site VPN architectures linking on-premise and cloud environments. Routing and BGP: Design, implement, and maintain complex routing architectures leveraging advanced protocols such as BGP and OSPF to ensure resilient, performant connectivity. DNS Architecture: Design, implement, and maintain DNS architecture across on-premise and cloud environments, ensuring scalability, resiliency, and security. Disaster Recovery Network Design: Design and maintain resilient network architectures supporting disaster recovery and business continuity. Network Management: Oversee configuration, management, and optimisation of network devices (routers, switches, firewalls, VPNs), ensuring network security and compliance with best practices. Automation and Tooling: Use Git, Terraform, Bash, and Ansible to automate and manage infrastructure and network configuration as code. Collaboration and Communication: Work with cross-functional teams to gather requirements, provide technical guidance, and ensure alignment with business objectives. Documentation and Best Practices: Develop and maintain documentation, diagrams, and SOPs for network and cloud architectures, promoting industry best practices and compliance. What we are looking for: Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field 3+ years of proven experience as a Systems Architect, Network Architect, Cloud Architect, or similar role in a complex IT environment Strong understanding of AWS Cloud security and infrastructure security, including network and server security Relevant certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Advanced Networking – Specialty, AWS Certified Solutions Architect, CCNP) are a plus Work Experience: Strong expertise in designing and implementing hybrid (on-premise and cloud) network architectures Strong, hands-on AWS network experience, particularly with Transit Gateways, ACLs, Network Firewalls, Cloud WAN, VPC connectivity, EKS networking, and Route 53 Hands-on experience with AWS Direct Connect and VPN Gateway architectures for hybrid connectivity Experience designing and implementing complex routing architectures, leveraging advanced protocols such as BGP and OSPF Strong knowledge of DNS architecture design, implementation, and management across on-premise and cloud environments Experience designing disaster recovery and business continuity network architectures Experience with load balancing technologies (e.g., AWS ALB/NLB or equivalent on-premise solutions) Experience with network monitoring and observability tooling (e.g., VPC Flow Logs, CloudWatch, NetFlow) Working knowledge of IPv6 In-depth knowledge of networking protocols, security principles, and best practices Strong familiarity with Git, including branching, automation workflows, and merging strategies Excellent skills in Terraform, Bash, and Ansible Strong background in Linux administration Understanding of microservice design and architectural patterns Experience with Kubernetes/EKS networking, including CNI plugins and service mesh In-depth knowledge of on-premises infrastructure, including servers, SAN/NAS storage devices, fibre channel networks, and backup infrastructures Proficiency in Active Directory administration, including domain management, group policies, LDAP, and SAML integrations Familiarity with virtualisation technologies (VMware, Hyper-V, etc.) and containerisation (Docker, Kubernetes) Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, with a collaborative mindset Other Requirements: Proven practical communication skills (written and verbal) to articulate platform architecture to other Architects (Area and Enterprise), Area Product Managers, and technical teams Adherence to best practices in documentation, testing, security, and efficient use of resources Experience with identity solutions Awareness of relevant regulatory and compliance frameworks (e.g., PCI-DSS, ISO 27001) as they apply to network and infrastructure security What we offer Much like riding a rollercoaster, sometimes life at Betsson can be lightning fast with twists and turns but always FUN! Then again, what else would you expect from a business 75% millennial and 1700 strong, spread across 7 offices with 900 based out of our Malta HQ alone! We recognise it may not be for the faint-hearted, but if you’re a go-getter, initiator and adrenaline junkie, always striving to push the boundaries and challenge yourself, then you’ll fit right in. Challenge accepted? By submitting your application, you understand that your personal data will be processed as set out in our Privacy Policy
